mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 5% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of FEDFUNDS > 5% periods, or FEDFUNDS decline reverses before 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly UNRATE falls below 4%, labor market slack increases, reducing expected wage growth and depressing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in <30% of UNRATE < 4% episodes, or UNRATE quickly rebounds above 4% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (household spending) of at least 2% followed by a rise in GDPC1 (goods orders) exceeding 5% in the same quarter predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong demand signals robust economic growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST[month] > HOUST[previous month] + 2% AND GDPC1[quarter] > GDPC1[previous quarter] + 5%
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to beat a 5% confidence interval around the mean of prior non-accelerated quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) reading above 112.0 triggers a regime shift where 5-day S&P 500 forward returns are on average positive due to expectations of supply-side expansion.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive 5-day windows with INDPRO > 112.0, 5-day returns remain non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4.0% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as lower rates encourage risk-on positioning.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% before 20 days, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the prior 30-day average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment) by over 10,000 in a month coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates labor market cooling and potential policy restraint.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in >50% of monthly PAYEMS declines >10,000, or job growth resumes before 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases of at least 3% in both HOUST and RSAFS (retail sales) predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as dual demand channels reinforce optimism.
candidate_trigger: HOUST[month] > HOUST[previous month] * 1.03 AND RSAFS[month] > RSAFS[previous month] * 1.03
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically significant vs. a baseline of single-demand proxies.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months, supply-side inflation pressures are expected, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as markets price in higher future rates.
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain positive in >50% of UNRATE > 6% episodes, or UNRATE declines before 60 days.
